import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 688
*Reference:*
- [erdosproblems.com/688](https://www.erdosproblems.com/688)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul, _A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory_. Ann. Discrete Math. (1980), 89-115.
-/

open Real Filter

namespace Erdos688

/--
Define $\epsilon_n$ to be maximal such that there exists some choice of congruence class $a_p$
for all primes $n^{\epsilon_n} < p \leq n$ such that every integer in $[1,n]$ satisfies at least
one of the congruences $\equiv a_p \pmod p$.
-/
def Erdos688Prop (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℕ → ℕ), ∀ (m : ℕ), 1 ≤ m → m ≤ n →
    ∃ (p : ℕ), p.Prime ∧ (n : ℝ)^ε < p ∧ p ≤ n ∧
      a p ≡ m [MOD p]

noncomputable def epsilonFunction (n : ℕ) : ℝ := sSup {ε : ℝ | Erdos688Prop n ε}

/--
Estimate $\epsilon_n$ - lower bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.i.lower_bound :
    (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) =O[atTop] epsilonFunction := by
  sorry

/--
Estimate $\epsilon_n$ - upper bound.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.i.upper_bound :
    epsilonFunction =O[atTop] (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ) := by
  sorry

/--
In particular, is it true that $\epsilon_n = o(1)$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    epsilonFunction =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (1 : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős claims in [Er80] (p. 106) that it is not difficult to prove
$\epsilon_n \gg \frac{\log\log\log n}{\log\log n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_688.variants.lglglg_over_lglg_is_big_o :
    (fun (n : ℕ) ↦ (log (log (log (n : ℝ)))) / (log (log (n : ℝ))))
      =O[atTop] epsilonFunction := by
  sorry

end Erdos688

reformulations.difference: The source's informal 'maximal' exponent is implemented as the supremum of feasible exponents, with totalized values at small inputs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This captures the intended optimal cutoff. For fixed n > 1, only finitely many primes are available, and changes in feasibility occur at critical values log(p)/log(n). The strict cutoff generally prevents attainment of the optimal value: for example, Lean verifies epsilonFunction 3 = log(2)/log(3), while that exponent is not feasible. Replacing the strict cutoff by a weak cutoff gives the same supremum; this equality was proved in the scratch file for every n > 1. Thus using a supremum is appropriate, not a missing maximality condition. Empty or unbounded initial cases receive the default value zero; Erdős's positive lower bound ensures feasibility eventually, and all four theorem statements are insensitive to finitely many initial values. The full finite-critical-value characterization was not formalized.

review.notes: Checked both definitions and all four theorems. The quantifier order, prime bounds, residue-class encoding, answer types/scopes, and asymptotic directions match the source. The live page remains open and records the stated lower bound as known. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors or warnings. They establish boundedness of admissible exponents for positive n, nonnegativity of epsilonFunction, boundary values at n=0,1,2,3,4, equivalence with a finite residue-representative encoding, and invariance under finite initial changes. Nonnegativity also confirms that the norm-based Big-O formulation expresses the intended lower bound. The reviewed file was not modified.
